title: Resolution independence of the derived tensor product
statement:
Fix a scheme $Y$, a commutative ring $A$, and complexes $K_1,K_2$ of $A_Y$-modules on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Let $q:P\to K_1$ and $q':P'\to K_1$ be quasi-isomorphisms with K-flat sources [def-weil-derived-tensor]. If a morphism of complexes $\alpha:P\to P'$ is supplied with $q'\alpha$ homotopic to $q$, then
$$\alpha\otimes1_{K_2}:P\otimes_AK_2\longrightarrow P'\otimes_AK_2$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. No such direct comparison morphism is asserted to exist. Without choosing a direct comparison, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$Q(P\otimes_AK_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(P'\otimes_AK_2)$$
in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, where $Q$ is the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It depends on the specified resolution maps $q,q'$, agrees with $Q(\alpha\otimes1_{K_2})$ whenever such an $\alpha$ is supplied, is the identity for identical resolutions, and satisfies the cocycle identity for three resolutions. Thus the object $K_1\otimes_A^LK_2$ of [def-weil-derived-tensor] is independent of the chosen K-flat resolution up to this canonical isomorphism.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism f and a K-flat complex R, the cone of f is acyclic. The definition of K-flatness makes Cone(f) tensor R acyclic. CochainComplex.mapBifunctorMappingCone₁Iso and the cone criterion prove f tensor 1_R is a quasi-isomorphism (private tensor_right_quasiIso). Tensor preadditivity is supplied by the existing SheafOfModules.tensorPreadditive API, and uses no boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tags 06YT and 06YU; two-factor resolution argument and right-calculus uniqueness

proof.text: For a K-flat first factor P and a quasi-isomorphism r, apply K-flatness to Cone(r). The componentwise braiding is an isomorphism of double complexes; totalization followed by HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorFlipIso gives the signed swap. Thus P tensor Cone(r) is acyclic. CochainComplex.mapBifunctorMappingCone₂Iso and the cone criterion prove 1_P tensor r is a quasi-isomorphism (private tensor_left_quasiIso).

source.place: Tags 06YT and 06YU; two-factor resolution argument and right-calculus uniqueness

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution r:R → K₂ by lem-pc-kflat-resolution. For each K-flat resolution q:P → K₁, Steps 1 and 2 make the maps P tensor R → K₁ tensor R and P tensor R → P tensor K₂ quasi-isomorphisms. Localize and invert the second map to obtain e(P,q):Q(P tensor K₂) ≅ Q(K₁ tensor R). Define c(P,P′) = e(P,q) followed by e(P′,q′) inverse. No new definition chooses an arbitrary witness: R is eliminated locally inside the proof of the proposition.

source.place: Tags 06YT and 06YU; two-factor resolution argument and right-calculus uniqueness

proof.text: For a supplied homotopy α ≫ q′ ~ q, homology and two-out-of-three make α a quasi-isomorphism. Apply Step 1 to α tensor 1_R. The naturality square for r and Step 2 make α tensor 1_K₂ a quasi-isomorphism by two-out-of-three. HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorMapHomotopy₁ sends the supplied homotopy to a tensor homotopy. DerivedCategory.Q_map_eq_of_homotopy and tensor functoriality give Q(α tensor 1_K₂) followed by e(P′,q′) equal to e(P,q). Cancellation proves agreement of c with the localized tensor map. Cancellation of e and its inverse proves identity and cocycle directly.

source.place: Tags 06YT and 06YU; two-factor resolution argument and right-calculus uniqueness

proof.text: For uniqueness, the right-calculus Ore axiom converts the left fraction formed by q and q′ in the homotopy category to a right fraction, giving maps s:M → P and f:M → P′ with s ≫ q homotopic to f ≫ q′ and s a quasi-isomorphism. Homology and two-out-of-three show f is a quasi-isomorphism. Resolve M by a K-flat S and compose to obtain quasi-isomorphisms a:S → P and b:S → P′ with homotopic composites (private common_refinement). For any competing comparison family, agreement fixes its values on a and b. Its cocycle law and cancellation of the comparison from S to P force its value from P to P′ to equal c. This uses only the Ore axiom, not the equality criterion for arbitrary localized fractions.
